subject.title: Workboard: improve stacked-card readability and human-approval visibility

question: Should Workboard represent human-approval/action-required cards as a first-class UI concept, a configurable prominent-label rule, or leave this to existing blocked status and labels?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract is not: the fix could be UI-local, metadata-driven, or a new plugin config surface, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default behavior.

options.title: Use existing metadata for a UI signal
options.body: Add an approval or human-action count/badge derived from current status, diagnostics, notifications, notes, or labels before introducing plugin config.

options.title: Add configurable prominent labels
options.body: Define a Workboard plugin config contract for label patterns or prominent-label rules, with docs and tests for the new user-visible config surface.

options.title: Keep generic blocked and labels
options.body: Defer first-class human-action UX and document the existing blocked/status/filter workflow as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Use existing metadata for a UI signal
recommendation.body: Add an approval or human-action count/badge derived from current status, diagnostics, notifications, notes, or labels before introducing plugin config.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the Workboard plugin and dashboard surface, making them the strongest history-backed owner for the product-surface choice.
